---
title: A video's lifecycle
description: The five states a video moves through, what moves it, and what a re-encode does to a video that is already playing.
icon: RefreshCw
---

A video has one of five statuses, in the asset's `status` field. The status
says whether it can play; the work of encoding (probing, transcoding,
packaging) is tracked on jobs, so a video that is ready stays ready while it
is encoded again.

## The states

| Status | What it means | Plays? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `waiting_upload` | The video exists and its playback IDs are made, but the file hasn't arrived. | No |
| `processing` | The file has arrived and is being encoded. | No |
| `ready` | An output is published. | Yes |
| `errored` | The upload, the import or the first encode failed. `error_code` says why. | No |
| `deleted` | The video was deleted. Its playback stopped at once. | No |

## What moves it

| From | To | When | Webhook |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (new) | `waiting_upload` | Your backend creates an upload with `POST /v1/uploads`. | |
| (new) | `processing` | Your backend imports a URL with `POST /v1/assets`. | |
| `waiting_upload` | `processing` | The upload is completed. | |
| `waiting_upload` | `errored` | The upload is cancelled (`upload_cancelled`) or sits idle for 24 hours (`upload_expired`). | `video.asset.errored` |
| `processing` | `ready` | The first output is written and published. | `video.asset.ready` |
| `processing` | `errored` | The import or the encode fails for good, for example `import_failed` or `unsupported_source`. | `video.asset.errored` |
| `errored` | `processing` | You re-encode it with `POST /v1/assets/{id}/reencode`, if its source was kept. | |
| `ready` | `ready` | A re-encode finishes, the title changes, a playback ID is published, or the files move storage. | `video.asset.updated` |
| any | `deleted` | You delete it with `DELETE /v1/assets/{id}`. | `video.asset.deleted` |

The asset's `version` rises on every change. Webhooks are delivered at least
once and in no fixed order, so keep the highest `version` you have stored
and ignore an older snapshot. See [Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks).

## Re-encoding a ready video

`POST /v1/assets/{id}/reencode` encodes the source again, for example with
other [renditions](/docs/build/upload/renditions). The new encode writes a
new output beside the current one:

- The video stays `ready`, and viewers keep watching the current output.
- When the new output is complete, the video switches to it in one step and
  you get `video.asset.updated`. Players that start after that get the new
  output.
- If the re-encode fails, the current output keeps playing and you get
  `video.asset.reencode_failed`, with `job.error_code` saying why.

Only one job that changes a video runs at a time. A second re-encode while
one runs is `409 job_active`, with the running job's `job_id`; send
`"supersede": true` to cancel the running job and start yours. A delete
always wins: it cancels whatever is running.

A re-encode needs the source file. A video still `waiting_upload` has none
(`409 asset_not_ready`), and one whose source was not kept can't be encoded
again (`409 source_missing`).

## Tracks

Subtitles and chapters have their own status, on each track: `preparing`,
`ready` or `errored`. They are made after the video is ready and never hold
it up, so expect `video.asset.ready` first, then
`video.asset.track.ready` or `video.asset.track.errored`. See
[Subtitles and transcripts](/docs/build/captions/subtitles).
